# Voice test fixtures

## `kokoro_roundtrip.wav`

| | |
|---|---|
| **generated by** | `kokoro-onnx==0.6.1` |
| **model** | `kokoro-v1.0.int8.onnx` (sha256 `6e742170d309016e…`, 88 MB) |
| **voice pack** | `voices-v1.0.bin` (sha256 `bca610b8308e8d99…`, 26 MB) |
| **weights source** | `https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx/releases/download/model-files-v1.0/` |
| **retrieved** | 2026-09-03 |
| **voice** | `af_heart` |
| **spoken text** | `The meeting starts on Thursday and the client will review the design.` |
| **format** | WAV, 24 kHz, mono, 16-bit, 169,004 bytes |

Committed (169 KB) because it is the input to the round-trip wired gate, which
must run on a checkout that has **no** model weights. The weights themselves are
114 MB and are deliberately not committed — see `.gitignore` and Phase 5.

### Why this text, and why not the first one

The first attempt used **"The meeting starts at three fifteen on Thursday."**
with anchors `meeting` / `fifteen` / `thursday`. It **failed on `fifteen`**:
Whisper transcribed the spoken number as `"3 .15"`, so the transcript was
*correct* while the anchor was defeated by **numeral normalisation** — a known
ASR behaviour with nothing to do with what this gate tests.

The **fixture text** was changed, not the tolerance and not the anchor list.
Swapping anchors for whichever ones happened to pass would be cherry-picking
after the measurement; replacing a fixture whose content probes an unrelated
behaviour is a validity fix, the same class as excluding a Japanese posting from
an English-extractor measurement. Recorded here rather than silently corrected.

### The pinned gate

```
expected words : 12  (tolerance +/- 1)
content anchors: meeting, thursday, design
```

`±1` and not exact-match because Whisper on Kokoro on CPU is not deterministic;
an exact-string assertion would be a flaky test pretending to be a strict one.
Measured on the committed fixture at pin time: **12 words, exact transcript
match, all three anchors present.**
